topic: A passing check can still be wrong

items.prompt: Every test passes. What does that tell you?

correct.note: A test can only report what it looks at. The broken line in the example was never run.

covered.note: Passing says nothing about which lines ran. In the example one line ran under no test at all.

source.quote: A pass tells you the check found nothing. It does not tell you the check could have found it.

items.prompt: With suite size allowed for, how closely did coverage track catching faults across 31,000 suites?

choices.text: Closely: more coverage, more faults caught
Weakly to moderately, and near zero in one program

strong.note: Bigger suites both cover more and catch more. Once size was allowed for, most of the link went away.

inverse.note: The study found a weak link, not a reversed one.

source.quote: Their advice: coverage should not be used as a quality target.

items.prompt: What is a mutant in testing?

choices.text: A deliberate break in the code, to see whether the tests notice
A test that passes and fails at random
A patch written by an AI model

flaky.note: That is a flaky test. The film's term means a change made on purpose to the code under test.

ai.note: Patches came up in the next chapter. The term here means a change made on purpose to test the tests.

source.quote: The deliberate breaks are called mutants.

items.prompt: In the 2025 re-check of AI patches counted as solved, what share failed the developers' own tests?

none.note: Solved meant passed the benchmark's tests. Stronger tests written by the developers caught some that passed.

half.note: A larger share behaved differently from the real fix, which is a different measure.

source.quote: Seven point eight percent of the patches counted as solved failed the developers' own tests

choices.text: Asking a second model to agree
A known failure fed to the check, which must fail it

rerun.note: A rerun repeats any blind spot the check has. A control tests whether the check can fail at all.

second.note: Agreement from another model is a second opinion, not a test of whether the check can say no.

source.quote: That planted failure is a false-success control, and it costs one extra run.
